name: Russian Empire

areaKm2.note: world_1900 polygon "Russian Empire" = 21.54M km2 on the sphere; the Empire incl. Finland and Central Asia ~22.4M km2. Kwantung lease and the Chinese Eastern Railway zone excluded.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1904 = 141,600k (Empire incl. Finland). 1897 census 125.6M plus Finland ~2.6M, grown ~1.5% a year.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) Russia 1900 = 14.5%; 1897 census urban 13.4%. COW upop 1904 = 8,064k (cities 100k+) = 5.7%.

activePersonnel.note: Russo-Japanese War page: the entire Russian army in 1904 amounted to 1,200,000 men in 29 corps (Olender); in the Far East only ~95,000-100,000 at the outbreak. COW NMC v7 milper 1904 = 1,160,000. Plus navy ~65,000.

trainedReserves.note: Menning, Bayonets before Bullets (1992) ch. 6: reserve (zapas) of ~2.5-3M trained men, plus trained opolchenie of the first category. The war mobilised 1,365,000 in all (Russo-Japanese War page).

supportPersonnel.note: Field and fortress artillery ~150,000, engineers ~30,000, navy ~65,000, train, staff and fortress services ~35,000. Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess: Russia mobilised ~15M of ~170M (~9%) in 1914-17; the 1904 system and transport limits put the practical ceiling lower.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Line, grenadier, Guard, Siberian and fortress infantry; European corps 28,000 men with 112 guns, Siberian divisions only 3,400 men (Russo-Japanese War page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Mosin M1891 rifle, few machine guns

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: conscripts with 4-5 year service; older reservists filled the Far East units

count.note: Rifle brigades (strelki), incl. Finnish and East Siberian rifles.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Mosin rifle

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: better marksmanship than the line

count.note: Guard cuirassier regiments only; the 1882 reform turned the line cavalry into dragoons.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: ceremonial heavy cavalry

count.note: Dragoon regiments (~50,000) and Cossacks on active service (~60,000).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: dragoon rifles, Cossack lances

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: Mishchenko's raid on Yingkou (Jan 1905) failed

count.note: Educated guess: field guns of ~29 corps (European corps 112 guns each per the Russo-Japanese War page) plus reserve and Siberian batteries; M1900/1902 76 mm QF guns being issued.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: M1902 76 mm quick-firer superior to the Japanese Type 31

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: direct fire from exposed positions early in the war

count.note: Battleships, cruisers and destroyers. Conway's 1860-1905: ~20-22 battleships in service (7 at Port Arthur, Baltic and Black Sea squadrons, 4 Borodinos completing), 3 coast-defence battleships, ~8 armoured and ~15 protected cruisers = 35/45/55; plus ~70 destroyers. Port Arthur sortie of 10 August 1904: 6 battleships, 4 cruisers, 14 destroyers (page). Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: torpedo-boat destroyers moved from ships_minor.

quality.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers 0.55/0.6/0.7 (45) and destroyers 0.5/0.55/0.65 (70), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric rows: quality 0.5-0.75 and 0.5. Evidence: mixed designs, Tsesarevich and Retvizan modern; mixed destroyer classes

training.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers (45) and destroyers (70), both 0.35/0.4/0.5, role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: little gunnery practice; Second Pacific Squadron raw crews; poor night-fighting

count.note: Torpedo boats (~100) and gunboats. The ~70 destroyers moved to ships_major (was 140/180/250), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: mixed destroyer classes

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: poor night-fighting

count.note: Educated guess: Delfin (1903) and one or two experimental boats at the outbreak; more shipped to Vladivostok in 1904-05.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Kuropatkin and Alekseyev, divided authority, plan based on wrong estimates of Japanese strength (page)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: stubborn in defence (Port Arthur), reservists unwilling

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.25-0.5. Evidence: distant, unpopular war; 1905 revolution brewing

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: Mosin magazine rifle, QF field gun, few Maxims

armor.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: no armoured cars or helmets in service

fortification.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: Port Arthur concrete forts, held until January 1905

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: single-track Trans-Siberian, incomplete round Lake Baikal (page)

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: telegraph and field telephones, early naval wireless

isr.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: balloon detachments, weak cavalry reconnaissance

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID): Russia 1904 = 1,152; USSR-area series 1904 = 2,185. The two series disagree; mid between.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW NMC v7 milex (thousands of pounds): 1903 = 48,301, 1904 = 50,305; against a national product of ~1.3-1.4bn pounds (~13bn rubles) that is 3.5-4%; war costs mostly fell in 1905.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: industry ~20% of national product on the eve of 1914 (Gregory).

annualCohort.note: Analogue ratio of the France 1805 snapshot (males reaching military age ~0.75-1.05% per year) applied to ~141M; about 1.0-1.1M men were liable each year and ~450,000 taken.

artillery.note: Educated guess: Putilov, Obukhov and state arsenal field-gun output per year.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: battleships and cruisers completed per year at Petersburg and Nikolaev yards.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: macadamised chaussees of European Russia.

railKm.note: CHAT (https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta) railline Russia 1904 = 49,711 km; add Finnish railways (~3,000 km) and the Chinese Eastern Railway (~2,400 km), which CHAT appears to exclude.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Petersburg/Kronstadt, Riga, Libau, Reval, Odessa, Sevastopol, Nikolaev, Vladivostok, Arkhangelsk.

merchantTonnage.note: Registered merchant tonnage 667k tons (Russia 1904, CHAT dataset https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta, variable shipton_all) x 1.5 (range 1.3-1.6). CHAT tonnage is registered (largely net) tons, so this may understate deadweight.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: armies tied to the railway in Manchuria.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses of the Empire.

chokepoints: Bosporus and Dardanelles (closed to Russian warships)

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: depth and climate at home; Manchuria (where the war was fought) is not home soil.

notes: Snapshot = Russian Empire on 8 February 1904 (Japanese attack on Port Arthur), peacetime army. Population and territory = the Empire incl. Finland; Kwantung lease and the Chinese Eastern Railway zone listed as bases abroad; includes is empty. Personnel: standing army, Cossacks on active service and navy = active; zapas reserves = trainedReserves. Strength figures from the Russo-Japanese War page (Olender; Connaughton) and COW. Branch split, artillery count and naval totals are reconstructions (grade C/D).
